Roger](/wiki/Gol_D._Roger "Gol D. Roger")'s ultimate treasure known as the "One Piece", and take over his prior title. Luffy sets sail as captain of the [Straw Hat Pirates](/wiki/Straw_Hat_Pirates "Straw Hat Pirates"),[[Jp 15]](#cite_note-SHPirates-16) and is joined by [Roronoa Zoro](/wiki/Roronoa_Zoro "Roronoa Zoro"), a swordsman and former bounty hunter; [Nami](/wiki/Nami_(One_Piece) "Nami (One Piece)"), a money-obsessed thief and navigator; [Usopp](/wiki/Usopp "Usopp"), a sniper and compulsive liar; and [Sanji](/wiki/Sanji_(One_Piece) "Sanji (One Piece)"), an amorous but chivalrous cook. This measurement disregards distinctions between architectural and non-architectural extensions, and simply measures to the highest point, irrespective of material or function of the highest element.[[10]](#cite_note-:1-10)

This measurement is useful for [air traffic obstacle](/wiki/Air_traffic_obstacle "Air traffic obstacle") determinations, and is also a wholly objective measure. However, this measurement includes extensions that are easily added, removed, and modified from a building and are independent of the overall structure.

This measurement only recently came into use, when the [Petronas Towers](/wiki/Petronas_Towers "Petronas Towers") passed the Sears Tower (now named [Willis Tower](/wiki/Willis_Tower "Willis Tower")) in height. The former was considered taller because its spires were considered architectural, while the latter's antennae were not. This led to the split of definitions, with the Sears Tower claiming the lead in this and the height-to-roof (now highest occupied floor) categories, and with the Petronas claiming the lead in the architectural height category.

If the original [World Trade Center](/wiki/World_Trade_Center_(1973%E2%80%932001) "World Trade Center (1973–2001)") towers were still standing, the [North](/wiki/1_World_Trade_Center_(1971%E2%80%932001) "1 World Trade Center (1971–2001)") (1,728 feet (526.7 m), including the antenna) and [South](/wiki/2_World_Trade_Center_(1971%E2%80%932001) "2 World Trade Center (1971–2001)") Towers (1,377 feet (419.7 m)) would fall between numbers 11 and 37 on the current list (as it can be assumed the rebuilt One World Trade Center would have never been built).

The first feature film in colour was *Miss Stone*, a movie about a Protestant missionary in Ottoman Macedonia. It was released in 1958.
